subproblems.title: Stationarity tested on the radial field g(y)·y gives Euler's identity ∫(n·g + Dg(y)y) dμ_C = 0 (identity (H))
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ and let C be an n-varifold on ℝ^N (C : Varifold N n univ) which is stationary in ℝ^N (C.firstVariation X = 0 for every C¹ compactly supported vector field X) and satisfies p_S(y) = y for C-a.e. (y,S), where p_S = Grassmannian.project S. Let μ_C = C.weight = π_#C. Then for every C¹ function g : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support, ∫ (n·g(y) + Dg(y)(y)) dμ_C(y) = 0, where Dg(y) = fderiv ℝ g y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (C : Varifold N n (univ : Set (Euclidean N))), C.Stationary → (∀ᵐ z ∂C.measure, Grassmannian.project z.2 z.1 = z.1) → ∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ∫ y, ((n : ℝ) * g y + fderiv ℝ g y y) ∂C.weight = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (identity (H)); this is Simon Ch. 8, 3.5 specialised to V = C, x = 0 and a profile identically 1 on spt g, whose normal-defect term vanishes because y ∈ S for C-a.e. (y,S) and δC = 0.
Notation: μ := C.weight = (C.measure).map Prod.fst (Varifold.weight); for S : Grassmannian N n, S.1 is its projection matrix and p_S := Grassmannian.project S; Dg(y) := fderiv ℝ g y; for a vector field X, div_S X(y) := Varifold.tangentialDivergence X y S = trace(S.1 · jacobian X y), where jacobian X y = clmToMatrix (fderiv ℝ X y) is the coordinate matrix of DX(y); C.firstVariation X = ∫ div_S X(y) dC.measure(y,S); C.Stationary means C.firstVariation X = 0 for every X : Varifold.TestVectorField univ (a C¹ field with compact support and tsupport ⊆ univ).
Fix g : ℝ^N → ℝ which is C¹ with compact support.
1. (The radial test field.) Put X(y) := g(y)•y. X is C¹ as the product of the C¹ function g with the smooth identity map (ContDiff.smul with contDiff_id). If X(y) ≠ 0 then g(y) ≠ 0, so support X ⊆ support g, tsupport X ⊆ tsupport g, and X has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right); trivially tsupport X ⊆ univ. Hence X (with these three facts) is an element of Varifold.TestVectorField univ, and stationarity gives C.firstVariation X = 0, i.e. ∫ div_S X(y) dC.measure(y,S) = 0.
2. (Divergence of the identity field.) For every y and S, div_S(id)(y) = n. Indeed fderiv ℝ (fun z ↦ z) y is the identity continuous linear map (fderiv_fun_id), whose coordinate matrix is the identity matrix (LinearMap.toMatrix_id), so div_S(id)(y) = trace(S.1 · 1) = trace(S.1) = n by Grassmannian.trace_eq (the trace condition defining the Grassmannian subtype).
3. (Pointwise divergence of X.) g is differentiable at y (it is C¹) and so is the identity. The weighted product rule SimonGMT Varifold.tangentialDivergence_smul (Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter08/RadialFirstVariation.lean:257), applied with h = g and the identity field, gives for every (y,S)
   div_S X(y) = g(y)·div_S(id)(y) + Dg(y)(p_S(y)) = n·g(y) + Dg(y)(p_S y)   (by step 2).
   (Mathematically: DX(y)v = g(y)v + (Dg(y)v)·y, so trace(P_S ∘ DX(y)) = g(y)·trace(P_S) + trace(v ↦ (Dg(y)v)·P_S y) = n·g(y) + Dg(y)(P_S y), because the trace of the rank-one map v ↦ ℓ(v)w is ℓ(w). The module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.RadialFirstVariation is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch08.Submission; the formalisation may add the line `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.RadialFirstVariation` to GMT/Ch08/Submission.lean (extra imports of the pinned packages are permitted by the comparator), or re-derive this product rule exactly as in this parenthesis.)
4. (The radial hypothesis.) By hypothesis p_S(y) = y for C.measure-a.e. (y,S). Hence div_S X(y) = n·g(y) + Dg(y)(y) for C.measure-a.e. (y,S), and by integral_congr_ae and step 1,
   ∫ (n·g(z.1) + Dg(z.1)(z.1)) dC.measure(z) = ∫ div_S X dC.measure = C.firstVariation X = 0.
5. (Transfer to the weight.) φ(y) := n·g(y) + Dg(y)(y) is continuous: g is continuous, y ↦ Dg(y) is continuous because g is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv), and evaluation (L, v) ↦ L v of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous (Continuous.clm_apply). So φ is strongly measurable and Prod.fst is measurable, and the change-of-variables formula for image measures (integral_map) gives ∫ φ dμ = ∫ φ d((C.measure).map Prod.fst) = ∫ φ(z.1) dC.measure(z). By step 4 this equals 0, i.e. ∫ ((n : ℝ)·g(y) + Dg(y)(y)) dC.weight(y) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: X(y) = g(y)•y is C¹ with compact support, hence a test field in K(ℝ^N;ℝ^N), so C.firstVariation X = 0 by stationarity.
div_S(id) = trace(S.1·1) = trace S.1 = n (Grassmannian.trace_eq), and tangentialDivergence_smul gives div_S X(y) = n·g(y) + Dg(y)(p_S y) for all (y,S).
p_S y = y for C-a.e. (y,S) turns 0 = ∫ div_S X dC into ∫ (n·g(y) + Dg(y)(y)) dC(y,S) = 0 (integral_congr_ae).
The integrand is continuous and depends on y only, so integral_map along Prod.fst rewrites it as ∫ (n·g + Dg(y)(y)) dC.weight = 0.

subproblems.title: Euler's identity for a locally finite measure implies the dilation law ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ = sⁿ ∫ g dμ for C¹_c functions
subproblems.statement: Let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N that is finite on compact sets and let n ∈ ℕ. Suppose that ∫ (n·h(y) + Dh(y)(y)) dμ(y) = 0 for every C¹ function h : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support (Dh = fderiv ℝ h). Then for every C¹ function g : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support and every s > 0, ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ g dμ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → (∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ∫ y, ((n : ℝ) * g y + fderiv ℝ g y y) ∂μ = 0) → ∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → ∫ y, g (s⁻¹ • y) ∂μ = s ^ n * ∫ y, g y ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof ((H) ⇒ (S) by differentiation under the integral sign and an ODE), with all constants made explicit.
Hypotheses: μ is a measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N (Borel σ-algebra) with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ), n ∈ ℕ, and
 (H) ∫ (n·h(y) + Dh(y)(y)) dμ(y) = 0 for every C¹ function h : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support, where Dh(y) := fderiv ℝ h y.
Fix a C¹ function g : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support. We prove ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ g dμ for every s > 0.
0. (Integrability.) Every continuous f : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support is μ-integrable: it is bounded and vanishes outside a compact set of finite μ-measure (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
1. (Constants.) tsupport g is compact, hence bounded: choose R₀ with tsupport g ⊆ B_{R₀}(0) (closed ball) and put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0, so tsupport g ⊆ B_R(0). Dg is continuous (g is C¹) and vanishes outside tsupport g (if y ∉ tsupport g then g ≡ 0 near y, so Dg(y) = 0: fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport); thus Dg has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv) and is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Choose L ≥ 0 with ‖Dg(y)‖ ≤ L for all y.
2. (Dilates.) For t > 0 let g_t(y) := g(t⁻¹y). g_t is C¹ (g composed with the linear map y ↦ t⁻¹y) and has compact support (support g_t = t·support g; HasCompactSupport.comp_smul). By the chain rule Dg_t(y) = Dg(t⁻¹y) ∘ (t⁻¹·id), hence Dg_t(y)(y) = Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y). The function k_t(y) := Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y) is continuous and vanishes wherever Dg(t⁻¹y) = 0, so its support lies in the support of y ↦ Dg(t⁻¹y), which has compact closure (the dilate of the compact support of Dg); so k_t is continuous with compact support. For t > 0 define F(t) := ∫ g(t⁻¹y) dμ(y) and J(t) := ∫ Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y) dμ(y); by step 0 both integrands are μ-integrable.
3. ((H) for the dilates.) Applying (H) to h = g_t (t > 0) and substituting Dg_t(y)(y) = Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y) gives ∫ (n·g(t⁻¹y) + Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y)) dμ(y) = 0. Both summands are integrable (steps 0 and 2), so the integral splits (integral_add, integral_const_mul): n·F(t) + J(t) = 0 for every t > 0.
4. (Pointwise t-derivative.) Fix y. For t > 0 the map t ↦ t⁻¹y has derivative −t⁻²·y (derivative of inversion, hasDerivAt_inv, times the constant vector y), so by the chain rule t ↦ g(t⁻¹y) has derivative Dg(t⁻¹y)(−t⁻²y) = −t⁻²·Dg(t⁻¹y)(y) = −t⁻¹·Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y) at t.
5. (Differentiation under the integral sign.) Fix t₀ > 0 and let I := (t₀/2, 2t₀), an open neighbourhood of t₀ contained in (0,∞). Set Φ(t,y) := −t⁻¹·Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y) and b(y) := (2LR/t₀)·1_{B_{2t₀R}(0)}(y).
 (a) Domination: |Φ(t,y)| ≤ b(y) for every y and every t ∈ I. If t⁻¹y ∉ tsupport g, then Dg(t⁻¹y) = 0, so Φ(t,y) = 0 ≤ b(y) (b ≥ 0 because L, R, t₀ ≥ 0). If t⁻¹y ∈ tsupport g, then ‖t⁻¹y‖ ≤ R, so ‖y‖ = t·‖t⁻¹y‖ ≤ tR ≤ 2t₀R and b(y) = 2LR/t₀; moreover |Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y)| ≤ ‖Dg(t⁻¹y)‖·‖t⁻¹y‖ ≤ LR and t⁻¹ < 2/t₀ (as t > t₀/2), so |Φ(t,y)| ≤ (2/t₀)·LR = b(y).
 (b) b is μ-integrable: it is a constant times the indicator of the closed ball B_{2t₀R}(0), a measurable compact set of finite μ-measure.
 (c) For every t, y ↦ g(t⁻¹y) is continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable; y ↦ g(t₀⁻¹y) is integrable (step 0); y ↦ Φ(t₀,y) is continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable; and by step 4, for every y and every t ∈ I, t ↦ g(t⁻¹y) has derivative Φ(t,y) at t.
 By the dominated differentiation theorem (Mathlib hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le, Analysis/Calculus/ParametricIntegral.lean:286, with the neighbourhood I of t₀ and the bound b), F is differentiable at t₀ and F'(t₀) = ∫ Φ(t₀,y) dμ(y) = −t₀⁻¹·J(t₀) (integral_neg, integral_const_mul).
6. (The ODE.) By steps 3 and 5, for every t > 0 we have J(t) = −n·F(t), so F has derivative −t⁻¹·J(t) = n·F(t)/t at t.
7. (Integration of the ODE.) For t > 0 let G(t) := F(t)/t^n. Since t ↦ t^n has derivative n·t^{n−1} (hasDerivAt_pow) and t^n ≠ 0, the quotient rule (HasDerivAt.div) shows that G has derivative ((n·F(t)/t)·t^n − F(t)·n·t^{n−1})/(t^n)² at t. This derivative is 0: if n = 0 both terms of the numerator vanish; if n = m + 1 the numerator equals n·F(t)·(t^{m+1}/t − t^m) = 0. So G is differentiable with derivative 0 on the open preconnected set (0,∞) and is therefore constant there (IsOpen.is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero with isOpen_Ioi and isPreconnected_Ioi). Consequently, for every s > 0, F(s)/s^n = G(s) = G(1) = F(1)/1^n = ∫ g(1⁻¹y) dμ(y) = ∫ g dμ, and multiplying by s^n ≠ 0 gives ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = F(s) = s^n·∫ g dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix R > 0 with tsupport g ⊆ B_R(0) and L ≥ 0 with ‖Dg‖ ≤ L; set F(t) = ∫ g(t⁻¹y) dμ, J(t) = ∫ Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y) dμ (continuous compactly supported integrands).
(H) applied to the C¹_c dilate g(t⁻¹·), whose derivative at y applied to y is Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y), gives n·F(t) + J(t) = 0 for t > 0.
d/dt g(t⁻¹y) = −t⁻¹·Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y), dominated on (t₀/2, 2t₀) by (2LR/t₀)·1_{B_{2t₀R}(0)}; hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le gives F'(t₀) = −t₀⁻¹·J(t₀).
Hence F'(t) = n·F(t)/t on (0,∞); G(t) = F(t)/t^n has zero derivative on (0,∞), so G is constant and F(s) = s^n·F(1) = s^n ∫ g dμ.

subproblems.title: Mollification extends the dilation law ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ = sⁿ ∫ g dμ from C¹_c to C_c functions
subproblems.statement: Let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N that is finite on compact sets, n ∈ ℕ and s > 0. Suppose that ∫ h(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ h dμ for every C¹ function h : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support. Then ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ g dμ for every continuous function g : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (s : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → 0 < s → (∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ∫ y, g (s⁻¹ • y) ∂μ = s ^ n * ∫ y, g y ∂μ) → ∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → ∫ y, g (s⁻¹ • y) ∂μ = s ^ n * ∫ y, g y ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (extension of the dilation law from C¹_c to C_c by mollification), for the fixed s.
Hypotheses: μ is a measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N (Borel) with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K, n ∈ ℕ, s > 0, and
 (S¹) ∫ h(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ h dμ for every C¹ function h : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support.
Let g : ℝ^N → ℝ be continuous with compact support. We prove ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ g dμ.
1. (Estimate.) If K ⊆ ℝ^N is compact, h : ℝ^N → ℝ vanishes outside K and |h(y)| ≤ ε for all y, then |∫ h dμ| ≤ ε·μ(K), where μ(K) < ∞ is read as a real number. Indeed ∫ h dμ = ∫_K h dμ because h = 0 off K (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), and |∫_K h dμ| ≤ ε·μ(K) because μ(K) < ∞ and |h| ≤ ε on K (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const).
2. (Limit criterion.) Let K be compact and let G and F_k (k ∈ ℕ) be μ-integrable functions such that F_k − G vanishes outside K for every k and, for every ε > 0, |F_k(y) − G(y)| ≤ ε for all y and all sufficiently large k. Then ∫ F_k dμ → ∫ G dμ. Proof: given ε > 0, for all large k we have |F_k − G| ≤ ε/(μ(K)+1) everywhere, so by integral_sub and step 1, |∫ F_k dμ − ∫ G dμ| = |∫ (F_k − G) dμ| ≤ ε·μ(K)/(μ(K)+1) < ε.
3. (Mollifiers.) For k ∈ ℕ let φ_k be the smooth bump function ContDiffBump (0 : ℝ^N) with inner radius 1/(2(k+1)) and outer radius 1/(k+1) (0 < 1/(2(k+1)) < 1/(k+1)), and let ψ_k := φ_k.normed volume be its normalisation with respect to Lebesgue measure: ψ_k ≥ 0, ∫ ψ_k = 1, support ψ_k = the open ball of radius 1/(k+1) about 0 (ContDiffBump.support_normed_eq), and ψ_k is C^∞ with compact support (contDiff_normed, hasCompactSupport_normed). Let g_k := ψ_k ⋆ g be the convolution with respect to Lebesgue measure (MeasureTheory.convolution ψ_k g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume).
 (a) g_k is C¹ (indeed C^∞): ψ_k is smooth with compact support and g, being continuous, is locally integrable (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
 (b) Let K₁ := B_1(0) + tsupport g (closed unit ball plus the compact support of g), a compact set as the sum of two compact sets. Then support g_k ⊆ support ψ_k + support g ⊆ B_1(0) + tsupport g = K₁ (support_convolution_subset, and 1/(k+1) ≤ 1), so g_k has compact support. Also support g ⊆ K₁ (write y = 0 + y with 0 ∈ B_1(0)).
 (c) Uniform convergence: g is uniformly continuous, being continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). Given ε > 0 choose δ > 0 with |g(x) − g(y)| ≤ ε whenever |x − y| < δ, and k₀ ∈ ℕ with 1/(k₀+1) < δ (exists_nat_one_div_lt). For k ≥ k₀ and any y, every x in the open ball of radius 1/(k+1) about y satisfies |x − y| < 1/(k+1) ≤ 1/(k₀+1) < δ and hence |g(x) − g(y)| ≤ ε; since ψ_k ≥ 0 has integral 1 and is supported in that ball, ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le gives |g_k(y) − g(y)| ≤ ε. Thus |g_k(y) − g(y)| ≤ ε for all y and all k ≥ k₀.
4. (Hypothesis for the mollified functions.) By 3(a), 3(b) and (S¹), ∫ g_k(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ g_k dμ for every k.
5. (Passage to the limit.)
 (i) Apply step 2 with K = K₁, F_k = g_k and G = g: all are continuous with compact support, hence μ-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport, μ being finite on compacts); g_k − g vanishes outside K₁ by 3(b); the uniform estimate is 3(c). Hence ∫ g_k dμ → ∫ g dμ.
 (ii) Apply step 2 with K = s·K₁ (compact, the image of K₁ under y ↦ s·y), F_k(y) = g_k(s⁻¹y) and G(y) = g(s⁻¹y): these are continuous with compact support (composition with y ↦ s⁻¹y; HasCompactSupport.comp_smul), hence integrable; if y ∉ s·K₁ then s⁻¹y ∉ K₁ (otherwise y = s·(s⁻¹y) ∈ s·K₁), so F_k(y) = G(y) = 0 by 3(b); and |F_k(y) − G(y)| = |g_k(s⁻¹y) − g(s⁻¹y)| ≤ ε for k ≥ k₀ by 3(c) at the point s⁻¹y. Hence ∫ g_k(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) → ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ(y).
6. (Conclusion.) By step 4 the sequences (∫ g_k(s⁻¹y) dμ)_k and (s^n ∫ g_k dμ)_k coincide; by step 5 the first converges to ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ and the second (5(i) multiplied by the constant s^n) converges to s^n ∫ g dμ. Limits in ℝ are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique), so ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ g dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: If h vanishes off a compact K and |h| ≤ ε then |∫ h dμ| ≤ ε·μ(K); hence uniform convergence with a common compact support gives convergence of integrals.
g_k := (normalised ContDiffBump of radius 1/(k+1)) ⋆ g is C¹, supported in the fixed compact K₁ = B_1(0) + tsupport g, and g_k → g uniformly (dist_normed_convolution_le + uniform continuity).
The hypothesis gives ∫ g_k(s⁻¹y) dμ = s^n ∫ g_k dμ for every k.
Passing to the limit on both sides (supports in s·K₁ and K₁) and using uniqueness of limits gives ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ = s^n ∫ g dμ.

subproblems.title: Riesz uniqueness turns the C_c dilation law into μ(s·A) = sⁿ μ(A) for every set A
subproblems.statement: Let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N that is finite on compact sets, n ∈ ℕ and s > 0. Suppose that ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ g dμ for every continuous function g : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support. Then μ(s·A) = s^n μ(A) for every set A ⊆ ℝ^N (not necessarily measurable); in ℝ≥0∞: μ (s • A) = ENNReal.ofReal s ^ n * μ A.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (s : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → 0 < s → (∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → ∫ y, g (s⁻¹ • y) ∂μ = s ^ n * ∫ y, g y ∂μ) → ∀ A : Set (Euclidean N), μ (s • A) = ENNReal.ofReal s ^ n * μ A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–5 of the parent proof (uniqueness in the Riesz representation theorem, then exact evaluation of an image measure under a measurable equivalence), for the fixed s.
Hypotheses: μ is a measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N (Borel σ-algebra) with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K, n ∈ ℕ, s > 0, and
 (S⁰) ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ g dμ for every continuous g : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support.
Let A ⊆ ℝ^N be an arbitrary set (not necessarily measurable).
1. (The dilation.) T(y) := s⁻¹•y is a homeomorphism of ℝ^N with inverse y ↦ s•y (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero, as s⁻¹ ≠ 0), hence a measurable equivalence for the Borel σ-algebra (Homeomorph.toMeasurableEquiv). For every B ⊆ ℝ^N, T⁻¹(B) = {y : s⁻¹•y ∈ B} = s•B, since y = s•(s⁻¹•y) (Set.preimage_smul_inv₀).
2. (Regularity.) ℝ^N is a σ-compact, locally compact metric space with its Borel σ-algebra. μ is finite on compact sets, hence locally finite (isLocallyFiniteMeasure_of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts), hence regular (Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure). Put ν₁ := μ.map T and ν₂ := ofReal(s)^n • μ. ν₁ is regular as the image of a regular measure under a homeomorphism (Measure.Regular.map), and ν₂ is regular as a regular measure multiplied by the finite constant ofReal(s)^n (Measure.Regular.smul). (Both are finite on compact sets: ν₁(K) = μ(T⁻¹K) = μ(s•K) < ∞ because s•K is compact, and ν₂(K) = ofReal(s)^n·μ(K) < ∞.)
3. (Equal integrals.) Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ). Then
 ∫ f dν₁ = ∫ f(T y) dμ(y) = ∫ f(s⁻¹•y) dμ(y)   (change of variables along the measurable equivalence T: integral_map_equiv)
 = s^n·∫ f dμ   (hypothesis (S⁰), f being continuous with compact support)
 = (ofReal(s)^n).toReal·∫ f dμ   (s > 0, so (ofReal s ^ n).toReal = (ofReal s).toReal^n = s^n: ENNReal.toReal_pow, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal)
 = ∫ f dν₂   (integral_smul_measure).
4. (Riesz uniqueness.) Two regular measures on ℝ^N that give the same integral to every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) are equal (uniqueness in the Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem: Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported, MeasureTheory/Integral/RieszMarkovKakutani/Real.lean:412). By steps 2 and 3, ν₁ = ν₂.
5. (Arbitrary sets.) For the image of a measure under a measurable equivalence, evaluation is exact on every set, measurable or not: ν₁(A) = (μ.map T)(A) = μ(T⁻¹(A)) (MeasurableEquiv.map_apply). Hence, by step 1 and step 4,
 μ(s•A) = μ(T⁻¹(A)) = ν₁(A) = ν₂(A) = ofReal(s)^n·μ(A)   (Measure.smul_apply),
i.e. μ (s • A) = ENNReal.ofReal s ^ n * μ A. ∎
proof_key_steps: T(y) = s⁻¹•y is a homeomorphism, hence a measurable equivalence, and T⁻¹(B) = s•B for every set B.
μ, μ.map T and ofReal(s)^n•μ are regular (finite on compacts on the σ-compact metric space ℝ^N; Regular.map, Regular.smul).
For f ∈ C_c: ∫ f d(μ.map T) = ∫ f(s⁻¹y) dμ = s^n ∫ f dμ = ∫ f d(ofReal(s)^n•μ); Riesz uniqueness (ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported) gives μ.map T = ofReal(s)^n•μ.
MeasurableEquiv.map_apply evaluates on arbitrary A: μ(s•A) = (μ.map T)(A) = ofReal(s)^n·μ(A).
